description:
Elevation of a 100 mph signal pole with a mast arm, drawn with the arm projecting to the left of a vertical pole. A luminaire arm curves up and to the left from the pole top. The mast arm lies below it and carries three vertical three-section signal heads, drawn as rounded rectangles with three circles each. A horizontal dimension labeled Mast Arm Length runs from the outermost signal head to the pole centerline. Along the arm, F1 is the spacing between the first and second heads and F2 is the spacing between the second and third heads, with no numeric values given. A fourth, separate four-section signal head is drawn below the first head on a short stub of arm that is cut off with a break mark at the second head position, showing a four-section head option. A vertical dimension labeled Standard Height runs from grade to the top of the pole.

Metal tag on the mast arm: a rectangular tag reading LA-XX-X-XXX-XX, with a curved leader to the underside of the mast arm near the pole. Its fields are labeled TYPE, LOAD CASE, DESIGN WIND VELOCITY and ACTUAL MAST ARM LENGTH (FT).

Side-mounted indications on the pole: a three-section signal head and a pedestrian-style square indication are mounted on the side of the pole shaft below the mast arm, on the side opposite the mast arm. Two dash-dot reference lines from these heads lead across to the drill detail. Vertical dimensions from grade to the heads read 7'-6" (to the lower, square indication) and 11'-3" (to the upper three-section head). The Standard Height dimension line is the tallest one at the right.

Side view opposite of mast arm: an enlarged view of the pole shaft seen from the side opposite the mast arm, showing a vertical column of three holes on the pole centerline. Two small holes are called out as two 3/4 in. diameter holes (drill through) and one center hole is called out as a 2 1/4 in. diameter hole (drill 1 side only). The two small holes sit above and below the center hole. The dimension from the upper small hole to the center hole is 4 1/2 in., and the overall spacing between the two small holes is 9 in. The dash-dot lines from the signal head positions lead to this view.

Hand hole and metal tag at the base: a Hand Hole is shown on the pole shaft low on the pole with a curved leader. A second metal tag reading LA-XX-X-XXX-XX-XX is shown, with fields TYPE, LOAD CASE, DESIGN WIND VELOCITY, MAX. MAST ARM LENGTH (FT) and HEIGHT (FT). A curved leader runs from this tag to the hand hole.

Foundation: the pole stands on a base plate at grade over a rectangular cast-in-drilled-hole foundation drawn below the grade line, labeled CIDH Foundation, See Detail on Sheet 1.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, title 100 MPH Poles, sheet 2 of 2, drawing number S-52.1.6. Page number 32 appears below the sheet.
notes:
1. Title of detail: Side Mount Indications Drill Detail.
2. Mast arm length is measured from the pole to the outermost signal head. Signal head spacings are labeled F1 and F2, values not given on this sheet.
3. Side view opposite of mast arm: two 3/4 in. diameter holes (drill through) and one 2 1/4 in. diameter hole (drill 1 side only), spaced 4 1/2 in. and 9 in. as shown.
4. Metal tag on mast arm: LA-XX-X-XXX-XX, reading type, load case, design wind velocity, actual mast arm length (feet (FT)).
5. Metal tag at hand hole: LA-XX-X-XXX-XX-XX, reading type, load case, design wind velocity, maximum (MAX.) mast arm length (FT), height (FT).
6. Side-mounted indications are at 7'-6" and 11'-3" above grade.
7. Cast-in-drilled-hole (CIDH) foundation: see detail on sheet 1.
title: 100 MPH Poles (Sheet 2 of 2): Side Mount Indications Drill Detail
summary: Shows how a 100 mph signal pole is drilled for side-mounted signal indications and tagged. A three-hole pattern on the side opposite the mast arm uses two 3/4 in. through holes and one 2 1/4 in. hole, spaced 4 1/2 in. and 9 in. Side-mounted indications sit at 7'-6" and 11'-3" above grade. Metal tags give the pole type, load case, design wind velocity, mast arm length and height.

description:
Elevation views: two pole elevations side by side, Type C-1-100 Pole at left and Type C-2-100 Pole at right. Both are 45 foot tapered steel poles for CCTV cameras, standing on a CIDH foundation drawn below a hatched grade line, with the foundation labeled See Foundation Detail, Sheet 2.

Type C-1-100 pole: pole height is 45'-0" with 12.125" base outside diameter (O.D.), 5.938" top O.D. and 0.4184" wall thickness (THK.). At the pole top, a Top-Mount Option (see Pan and Tilt Mounting Flange Detail, sheet 2) is shown, together with a Side-Mount Option (see Clamp and Side Mounted Camera Arm Detail, sheet 2), which is a horizontal camera arm 12' max. long projecting from the top of the pole. An Upper Handhole and Coupling is called out near the top (see detail, sheet 2). A luminaire arm 15' max. projects from the pole near 29'-6" above grade, with the callout See Note 3. Optional heads (signal heads) are shown on the lower pole, with a handhole near the base. Vertical dimensions from grade: 7'-6", 11'-3", 29'-6" and 45'-0".

Type C-2-100 pole: same 45'-0" pole with 12.125" base O.D. and 5.938" top O.D., with 0.6250" wall thickness. It has the same top-mount and side-mount camera options, upper handhole and coupling, and 15' max. luminaire arm (See Note 3). In addition it has a signal mast arm 45' max. long projecting to the left from the pole at about 16'-0" above grade (See Note 4). Two signal heads are on the arm separated by a sign, with spacing F between the heads ("F" spacing, see Note 2). A street name sign hangs from the arm, called out as Street Name Sign, See S-486.0. Optional heads and a handhole are on the lower pole. Vertical dimensions from grade: 7'-6", 11'-3", 16'-0", 29'-6" and 45'-0".

Pole specifications: a list under the C-1 pole, given in the notes field.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Camera Poles (Case 4 Mast Arm Loading - 100 MPH Wind Speed), sheet 1 of 2, drawing number S-52.1.4B. Drawn 11-15-07, approved March 18, 2008 by Rita L. Robinson, General Manager. Structural approval signed by Shailesh Patel, S.E., Division Engineer, Structural Engineering Division, Bureau of Engineering, dated 11-29-07. Page number 33.
notes:
Pole specifications:
Base plate and flanges: ASTM A-36.
Shaft: steel of 48,000 PSI minimum yield after fabrication. Design yield of Fy = 48,000 PSI in order that Fu/Fy > 1.5.
Pipe: ASTM A-53 Grade B.
Anchor bolts: ASTM A-307.
Welds: all butt welds to be ground flush with base metal.
Longitudinal: butt weld by the submerged arc process.
Circumferential: butt weld with permanent back-up ring.
Finish pole: hot-dip galvanized per ASTM A-123.
Finish hardware: hot-dip galvanized per ASTM A-153.

General notes:
1. Fabrication of the standards, luminaire arms and mast arms must conform to the 2006 Department of Transportation, State of California Standard Plans.
2. Refer to LADOT Standard Drawing No. S-52.1.6 for "F" spacing.
3. Projected luminaire arm length to be determined by Department of Public Works, Bureau of Street Lighting. Refer to Caltrans Standard Drawing No. ES-7C for luminaire arm connection detail.
4. Signal arm connection shall be for 45 ft. arm (Case 4 arm loading), as per Caltrans Standard Drawing No. ES-7F. Shorter arms may be used, as appropriate.
title: Camera Poles (Case 4 Mast Arm Loading - 100 MPH Wind Speed), Sheet 1 of 2
summary: Sheet 1 of 2 of drawing S-52.1.4B for 45 foot CCTV camera poles, Types C-1-100 and C-2-100, with top-mount or side-mount camera options, optional signal heads, a 15 ft max. luminaire arm and a handhole. Type C-2-100 also carries a 45 ft max. signal arm with a street name sign. Gives pole dimensions, wall thickness, steel and finish specifications and general notes.

description:
Pan and tilt mounting flange detail: a plan and an elevation of the top-mount camera flange. The plan shows a 6 1/2 in. diameter (ASTM A-36) round plate with 4 stainless steel studs, 3/8 in. diameter, equally spaced on a 4 3/4 in. diameter bolt circle (B.C.). The elevation shows a 1/2 in. plate welded to the pipe top with a 1/4 in. fillet weld, 4 NF threads with stainless nuts and bolts, and studs projecting 1 1/4 in. above the plate.

Upper handhole and coupling detail: a section through the pole shaft near the top. A 2 in. coupling is welded on one side with a 1/4 in. weld, and a 3 in. x 5 in. handhole rim (1/4 in. plate x 2 in. wide) and cover is welded on the opposite side with 1/4 in. welds. The coupling and handhole are located 18 in. from the pole top. A cable hook, welded to the inside of the shaft, is oriented directly opposite the coupling and above the handhole. A footnote marked with an asterisk explains cable support.

Clamp and side mounted camera arm detail: a plan and elevation of the side-mount arm. A 3 in. Schedule 40 pipe (hot-dip galvanized per ASTM A-153) runs up to 12' max. between a clamp on the pole and a 6 1/2 in. diameter x 1/2 in. thick plate (ASTM A-36) at the camera end. The clamp consists of a 1/2 in. U bolt (ASTM A-307) and a 3/8 in. plate clamp, with 1/4 in. fillet welds. The end plate has 4 stainless steel studs, 3/8 in. diameter, equally spaced on a 4 3/4 in. diameter B.C. In elevation the pipe end plate is a 1/2 in. plate with 1/4 in. gusset plates on each side and 1/4 in. welds, 2 places.

Base plate detail: plan of an 18 in. x 18 in. square base plate with rounded corners, a center hole with diameter equal to the pole inside diameter minus 2 in., and 4 holes equally spaced on an 18 in. diameter bolt circle at the corners. Diagonal offset dimensions of 3 in., 1 1/2 in. and 2 3/8 in. are given for the bolt hole pattern.

Foundation detail: section through the CIDH foundation, 36 in. wide and 10' deep. A base plate 18 in. x 18 in. x 1.75 in. sits at finished grade on a 4 in. topping, with a 4 1/2 in. dimension at the top. Four anchor bolts, 2 in. x 42 in. x 6 in., each with 2 nuts and 2 washers (one above and one below the plate), are cast in. A bonding strap or wire is shown under the plate. The dimension between conduits is 12 2/5 in. Three conduits enter the foundation: 3 in. conduit (traffic), 1 in. conduit (BSL) and 2 in. conduit (CCTV cable). A reinforcing cage is drawn in the lower part of the foundation, 32 in. cage diameter and 9'-6" cage depth, see detail of Section A-A in LADOT Std. Dwg No. S-52.1.6.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Camera Poles (Case 4 Mast Arm Loading - 100 MPH Wind Speed), sheet 2 of 2, drawing number S-52.1.4B. Page number 34.
notes:
Pan and tilt mounting flange detail: 4 - 3/8 in. diameter stainless steel studs, equally spaced on 4 3/4 in. diameter B.C. 6 1/2 in. diameter (ASTM A-36). 4 NF threads, stainless nuts and bolts. 1/2 in. plate. 1 1/4 in. 1/4 in. fillet weld.

Upper handhole and coupling detail: 2 in. coupling. 18 in. from pole top. Cable hook* welded to inside of shaft oriented directly opposite coupling and above handhole. 3 in. x 5 in. handhole rim (1/4 in. plate x 2 in. wide) and cover. 1/4 in. welds.
* Each cable shall be supported inside the pole by Kellems grips (or equivalent) one at the top and a second at the mid-point. Two 1/8 in. diameter galvanized steel wires shall secure mid-point grips to the top cable hook.

Clamp and side mounted camera arm detail: 3 in. Schedule 40 pipe (hot-dip galvanized per ASTM A-153). 1/2 in. U bolt ASTM A-307. 3/8 in. plate clamp. 6-1/2 in. diameter x 1/2 in. thick plate (ASTM A-36). 12' max. 4 - 3/8 in. diameter stainless steel studs, equally spaced on 4 3/4 in. diameter B.C. 1/2 in. plate. 1/4 in. gusset plate each side. 1/4 in. welds, 2 places.

Base plate detail: 18 in. x 18 in. Hole diameter = pole inside diameter - 2 in. 4 holes, equally spaced on 18 in. diameter B.C. Diagonal offset dimensions 3 in., 1 1/2 in., 2 3/8 in.

Foundation detail: finished grade. Base plate 18 in. x 18 in. x 1.75 in. 4 in. topping. 4 1/2 in. (4)2 in. x 42 in. x 6 in. anchor bolts with 2 nuts and 2 washers per bolt (one above and one below the plate). Bonding strap or wire. 12 2/5 in. 3 in. conduit (traffic). 1 in. conduit (BSL). 2 in. conduit (CCTV cable). Foundation 36 in. wide, 10' deep. Reinforcing cage: 32 in. cage diameter, 9'-6" cage depth, see detail of Section A-A in LADOT Std. Dwg No. S-52.1.6.

Foundation design criteria: wind load design based on 2001 AASHTO Standard Specifications for Structural Support for Highway Signs, Luminaires, and Traffic Signals. (Fatigue requirements of Chapter 11 are not considered.) Wind speed = 100 mph.

Notes:
1. Bar reinforcement shall conform to ASTM A615 Grade 60.
2. All soils supporting and surrounding the foundation shall be undisturbed natural soil or 90% compacted fill.
3. Foundation concrete shall be 560-C-3250.
title: Camera Poles (Case 4 Mast Arm Loading - 100 MPH Wind Speed), Sheet 2 of 2
summary: Sheet 2 of 2 of drawing S-52.1.4B gives the camera pole details: pan and tilt mounting flange, upper handhole and coupling, clamp and side mounted camera arm, 18 in. base plate and the 36 in. by 10 ft CIDH foundation. The foundation carries a 32 in. reinforcing cage and three conduits. Design criteria and three foundation notes are included.

description:
Typical installation elevations, not to scale, of two BSL (Bureau of Street Lighting) poles with a Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon (RRFB) sign arm. The left pole is BSL Poles (CD953A, CD953B, CD953C) and the right pole is BSL Poles (CD953-A2, CD953-B2, CD953-C2). Both are drawn identically except the left pole has a single luminaire arm curving to the left and the right pole has two luminaire arms curving left and right.

Upper pole: a pole-top finial sits above a luminaire arm. A solar panel is mounted on a short arm on the pole with the note Tilt solar panel to 60 deg and rotate assembly so collector panel will face due south. Two horizontal arms project to the left, each at most 8' max. from the pole, attached to the pole by clamps called out as Detail D. The arms carry a W11-2 pedestrian crossing sign, shown as a diamond with walking figure, mounted between them, with RRFB lights below the sign, called out as Detail B (Back to Back). The bottom of the RRFB assembly is at 17' min. above grade, shown by a vertical dimension with a break symbol.

Lower pole: below a break, a Control Cabinet is mounted on the pole. Below it is a W11-2(2) pedestrian crossing sign, with RRFB's (Back to Back) below it, and a W16-7p(2) supplemental arrow plaque below the RRFBs. A Pedestrian Pushbutton is mounted on the pole, with dimensions of 42 in. from grade to the pushbutton level and 84 in. from grade to the bottom of the W16-7p(2) plaque level. The pole base has a base plate on a concrete foundation with a sidewalk or pad stepped to the left, with a 36 in. dimension from the pole centerline to the edge of the pad. Callout: Foundation Details, See Sheet 4.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, BSL Poles with Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon Sign Arm, sheet 1 of 4, drawing number S-52.1.7. Drawn by AC 01-22-20, TE SB 09-03-20, Sr. TE JV 09-03-20, approved 9-18-20 for Seleta J. Reynolds, General Manager. Structural design checked by Vigen Gharibian, SE and approved by Shailesh Patel, SE, Division Engineer, Structural Engineering Division, dated 9-04-20. Bureau of Engineering, Gary Lee Moore, PE, ENV SP, City Engineer. Page number 35.
notes:
1. Tilt solar panel to 60 degrees and rotate assembly so collector panel will face due south.
2. Arm projection 8' max. from the pole.
3. Signs and devices: W11-2(2), RRFB's (back to back), W16-7p(2), pedestrian pushbutton, control cabinet. Detail B (back to back), Detail D.
4. Dimensions: 17' min. above grade to the bottom of the upper RRFB assembly, 42 in. and 84 in. heights above grade at the pushbutton and W16-7p(2) levels, 36 in. from the pole centerline to the pad edge.
5. Foundation details: see sheet 4.
6. Typical installation. Not to scale.
title: BSL Poles with Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon Sign Arm (Sheet 1 of 4)
summary: Typical installation of Bureau of Street Lighting poles carrying a rectangular rapid flashing beacon sign arm, drawing S-52.1.7. Shows the single luminaire arm poles CD953A, B and C and the twin-arm poles CD953-A2, B2 and C2, each with an 8 ft max. sign arm, W11-2 signs, RRFBs, a control cabinet, solar panel and pushbutton. Foundation details are on sheet 4.

description:
Detail B (Not to scale): a front elevation and a side elevation of the back-to-back W11-2 pedestrian crossing sign on the RRFB sign arm. The side view at left shows two parallel vertical members with clamps, a round pole section at top and bottom, and RRFB light bars hanging at the outer lower corners, with a callout to Detail C at the lower clamp. The front view shows a diamond W11-2 sign with a walking figure held between two horizontal sign arms, with RRFB bars below, and the arms extending to the right to the pole with clamped connections. A dimension reads 8' max. from the pole to the free end of the arms, with a break symbol in the dimension line.

Detail C (Not to scale): a 3D exploded view of a Pelco AB-3004 pole band and bracket assembly, showing a clamp bracket, two U bolts with nuts, and two steel straps. It is labeled (PELCO AB-3004).

Table 1, Sign arm data, columns arm span "L" (FT.), fixed end diameter (IN), free end diameter (IN), gauge (GA.), degree rise: one row, 8'-0", 3.52, 2.4, 11, 0.50.

Table 2, Sign arm material data, columns component, ASTM designation, minimum yield (KSI): sign arm shaft, A595 GR. A, 55. Clamp, A572, 55. Sign arm connection bolts, A325, 55. Hardware coating, hot dip zinc, no yield given.

Table 3, Finish notes: system galvanized (GV). Base coat hot dip galvanized to ASTM A123. Prime coat none. Color none. Finish coat none.

Table 4, Sign dimensions, columns sign designation, sign or plaque, conventional road single lane, multi-lane: W11-2 pedestrian, 30x30*, 36x36. W16-7p downward diagonal arrow, 24x12, 24x12. Footnote marked with an asterisk below the table.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon Sign Arm, sheet 2 of 4, drawing number S-52.1.7. Page number 36.
notes:
1. Detail B and Detail C are not to scale.
2. Maximum (max.) sign arm length is 8'.
3. Sign arm data: arm span L 8'-0", fixed end diameter 3.52 in., free end diameter 2.4 in., gauge 11, degree rise 0.50.
4. Sign arm material data: sign arm shaft ASTM A595 Grade A, 55 ksi minimum yield. Clamp ASTM A572, 55 ksi. Sign arm connection bolts ASTM A325, 55 ksi. Hardware coating hot dip zinc.
5. Finish notes: system galvanized (GV). Base coat hot dip galvanized to ASTM A123. Prime coat none. Color none. Finish coat none.
6. Sign dimensions in inches (conventional road, single lane / multi-lane): W11-2 pedestrian 30x30* / 36x36. W16-7p downward diagonal arrow 24x12 / 24x12.
* The minimum size required for diamond-shaped warning signs facing traffic on multi-lane conventional roads shall be 36x36 per MUTCD section 2C.04.
Detail C: (Pelco AB-3004).
title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon Sign Arm (Sheet 2 of 4), Drawing S-52.1.7
summary: Sheet 2 of 4 of drawing S-52.1.7 gives the 8 ft max. RRFB sign arm data, including diameters, gauge and rise, plus material, finish and sign size tables. Detail B shows the back-to-back W11-2 sign assembly and Detail C shows the Pelco AB-3004 clamp. Sign sizes are 30x30 or 36x36 for W11-2 and 24x12 for the W16-7p arrow.

description:
Detail D, Sign arm attachment (Not to scale): elevation of a single sign arm tapering from a fixed end at the pole to a free end at the left. The arm is 8'-0" max. long. The free end has a removable cap and a diameter of 2.4 in. (free end diameter 2.4"). The fixed end has a diameter of 3.52 in. (fixed end diameter 3.52") and ends in a clamp plate called out as Detail E.

Sign arm attachment data table: clamp range (diameter) and dimension A: 3.75"-5.00", 7.08". 4.75"-6.00", 8.24". 5.75"-7.00", 9.36". 6.75"-8.00", 10.42". 7.75"-9.00", 11.49". 8.75"-10.00", 12.59". 9.75"-11.00", 13.64". 10.75"-12.00", 14.64". 11.75"-13.00", 15.71". 12.75"-14.00", 16.74". 13.75"-15.00", 17.77". 14.75"-16.00", 18.79". 15.75"-17.00", 19.81".

Detail E (Not to scale): three views of the clamp. The top view shows the clamp wrapped around the pole with 2 bolts and a cotter pin at the anti-rotation pin. The front view shows the 2 clamp halves with 4 hex bolts at dimension A across (bolt spacing), a 4 in. vertical bolt spacing, a 6 in. overall clamp height and a central 1.25 in. diameter wiring access hole. The side view shows a bolt spacing of 3 in. and plate thickness 0.313 in. minimum.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon Sign Arm, sheet 3 of 4, drawing number S-52.1.7. Page number 37.
notes:
1. Removable cap at the free end. Arm length 8'-0" max.
2. Fixed end diameter 3.52 in. Free end diameter 2.4 in.
3. (4) 0.50 in. diameter hex bolt with (1) hex head (HH) nut, (2) flat (FL) washers and (1) lock (LK) washer per bolt.
4. Hole in pole for 0.63 in. x 2 in. anti-rotation pins to be field drilled.
5. 0.13 in. x 1.50 in. cotter pin (holds anti-rotation pin in place).
6. 1.25 in. diameter wiring access hole in pole shaft to be field drilled.
7. Detail E: 0.313 in. thick minimum. Bolt spacing 4 in. and 3 in., clamp height 6 in.
8. Dimension A is taken from the sign arm attachment data table for the pole diameter.
title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon Sign Arm (Sheet 3 of 4), Drawing S-52.1.7
summary: Sheet 3 of 4 of drawing S-52.1.7 shows how the tapered 8 ft max. RRFB sign arm attaches to a pole with a four-bolt clamp. A table gives dimension A for clamp ranges from 3.75 in. to 17.00 in. pole diameter. Detail E gives the clamp plate dimensions, anti-rotation pin and field-drilled wiring access hole.

description:
Plan view of the foundation (top): a 36 in. diameter footing (minimum 3000 psi concrete) drawn as a circle, with an 11 1/2 in. bolt circle and four anchor bolts at an 8 1/8 in. square pattern. A 45 degree angle is shown at each of two radial lines on the right side. Conduit stubs project radially from the footing at the right and bottom, with a conduit cluster at the center.

Section view (bottom): a section through the foundation and sidewalk topping. The footing is 36 in. wide and 60 in. deep. A topping at least 4 in. thick sits on top of the footing, with the sidewalk or pad stepped to the left and 36 in. from the pole centerline to the pad edge. A bushing sits 2 3/4 in. above the topping. A bonding strap or wire is shown at the pole. Reinforcement is (8) #10 long reinforced bars with #4 ties at 9 in. on center (OC), typical (TYP.), provide (2) ties at 2 in. OC at top. Clearances of 3 in. and 2 in. are called out at the left side and 3 in. clear at the bottom. Anchor bolts are 1 1/8 in. x 40 in. x 4 in., 2 nuts and 2 washers per bolt, ASTM F1554 Grade 55 bolts. A 1 in. diameter street light conduit and a 2 in. diameter traffic signal conduit enter the footing, the traffic signal conduit stubbing out 6 in. min. beyond the footing face. A 14 in. min. dimension is shown on the right side at the upper part of the footing.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Foundation Details, sheet 4 of 4, drawing number S-52.1.7. Page number 38.
notes:
1. Use 1 in. galvanized conduit for street lighting and 2 in. schedule 80 PVC conduit for traffic signal unless otherwise specified.
2. Conduit stubs from foundation shall be in the direction of the nearest corresponding pullbox unless otherwise specified.
3. Topping shall be considered as a part of the foundation.
4. Coordinate bolt circle with light pole base plate prior to anchor bolt installation.
5. Coordinate conduit size and placement with electrical prior to installation.
Callouts: 36 in. diameter footing (minimum 3000 psi concrete). 11 1/2 in. bolt circle. 8 1/8 in. square. Bonding strap or wire. Bushing. 4 in. min. topping. (8) #10 long reinforced. 1 in. diameter street light conduit. 2 in. diameter traffic signal conduit. Anchor bolts 1 1/8 in. x 40 in. x 4 in. (2 nuts and 2 washers required per bolt) (ASTM F1554 Grade 55 bolts). #4 ties at 9 in. OC, typical (provide (2) ties at 2 in. OC at top).
title: Foundation Details (Sheet 4 of 4), Drawing S-52.1.7
summary: Sheet 4 of 4 of drawing S-52.1.7 gives the foundation for the BSL pole with RRFB sign arm. It is a 36 in. diameter, 60 in. deep footing with a 4 in. min. topping, eight #10 bars, #4 ties at 9 in. and four 1 1/8 in. anchor bolts on an 11 1/2 in. bolt circle. It shows 1 in. street light and 2 in. traffic signal conduit and five notes.

description:
Platform, top view detail (not to scale): a 36 in. x 36 in. square steel platform in plan. Four circles mark the four 5 gallon cans filled with concrete, one near each corner. A Type 1 base sits at the center of the platform with 4 bolts, and a 3/8 in. diameter steel coil chain is run through each can and locked around the Type 1 standard.

Platform, bottom view detail (not to scale): 36 in. x 36 in. in plan, with steel angle brackets crossing the underside as a framed grid. 4 holes at 1-1/4 in. diameter are laid out on an 8-1/2 in. diameter bolt circle at the center. 1 in. x 1 in. notches for cable are cut at the perimeter lip near the lower right corner.

Elevation: a temporary signal on a Type 1 standard. A signal head with three 12 in. sections, a second three-section head on a mast arm, a street name sign, and a pedestrian signal head (hand and walking person) are mounted on the pole. At the bottom, two 5 gal. concrete blocks sit on the platform and are chained around the Type 1 standard. The base assembly is bolted to the platform, which has a 2 in. high lip. Callouts: 1 in. x 1 in. notch for cable, LADOT name on the platform. A note beside the plate says for slopes greater than 1/2 in. rise per foot, the temporary standard is to be set level through the use of grading or wood shims.

Weight block (not to scale): a 5 gal. can filled with concrete, 12 in. wide by 14 in. tall, with a 1/2 in. diameter steel rod loop at the top embedded 9 in. deep, the loop 4 in. wide and projecting 3 in. above the can. Minimum weight is 90 lbs. LADOT or contractor name is embossed or welded on at least two sides.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Temporary Signal for Type 1 Standard, sheet 1 of 1, drawing number S-57.2B, drawn 3-1-16, approved 4-11-16 by Seleta J. Reynolds, General Manager. Page number 39.
notes:
1. Use 12 in. heads corresponding to permanent heads being replaced.
2. 36 in. square (SQ.) x 1/4 in. thick (THK.) steel platform, hot dip galvanized per ASTM 123.
3. Type 1 base with 4 1 in. diameter x 3-1/2 in. bolts and nuts with 2 washers for each bolt.
4. 3/8 in. diameter steel coil chain tied to each 5 gal. block and locked around the Type 1 standard.
5. 5 gal. can filled with concrete. Four cans are required, spaced as shown.
6. 2 in. high x 1/4 in. thick perimeter lip resting on ground.
7. 1-3/4 in. x 1-3/4 in. x 1/4 in. steel angle brackets welded to plate.
8. 4 holes at 1-1/4 in. diameter. 8-1/2 in. diameter bolt circle.
9. 1 in. x 1 in. notches for cable.
10. For slopes greater than 1/2 in. rise per foot, temporary standard to be set level through the use of grading or wood shims.
11. Weight block: 5 gal. can filled with concrete, minimum weight 90 lbs. 1/2 in. diameter steel rod embedded 9 in. deep. 'LADOT' or contractor name embossed or welded on at least two sides.
title: Temporary Signal for Type 1 Standard
summary: Drawing S-57.2B shows a temporary signal on a Type 1 standard held by a 36 in. square steel platform and four 5 gallon concrete-filled cans chained around the pole. It gives the platform plan and underside layout, bolt circle, lip, notches and a weight block detail of at least 90 lbs. It requires leveling on slopes steeper than 1/2 in. per foot.

description:
Plan view: a 60 in. x 60 in. square footing assembly seen from above, made of precast concrete blocks laid in a 3 x 3 grid around the pole. Four 23 in. x 23 in. x 30 in. precast concrete blocks (4 req.) sit at the corners and four 23 in. x 13 in. x 30 in. precast concrete blocks (4 req.) sit at the middle of each side, with the pole in the center square. A 6 in. dimension is shown at the edge of the center block and a 6 in. dimension at the side. Steel angles 5 in. x 3 in. x 1/2 in. (typical) are shown at the corners and side midpoints, called out as weld angles to plate (revision 1 mark). A dashed square marks a 3/8 in. coil chain that ties the blocks together. A 2 in. hole is called out at the pole center. Four holes are drilled to accommodate a 1-1/8 in. bolt size on an 11-1/2 in. bolt circle. Section marks A and A are shown on the left and right of the plan.

Elevation: a Type CD954 standard (without luminaire arm) on a temporary base at the roadway. A mast arm up to 15'-0" max. long reaches left from the pole and carries one all-12 in. section signal head at its end. The signal head has three circles with two arrows in the lower rows. Temporary overhead (O.H.) signal wires with a maximum span of 100 feet are looped at the pole top. A vertical dimension of 17'-6" min. runs from the roadway to the bottom of the mast arm head. On the pole are 2 signal heads, each with five 12 in. sections (three round, two arrow), a street name sign, and 2 pedestrian heads. A callout reads See Plan and Section A-A, pointing at the base plate.

Section A-A: a vertical cut through the base. A 60 in. x 60 in. x 3/4 in. steel plate sits on an A.C. or P.C.C. surface over a mortar leveling bed. Blocks stand 30 in. high on the plate, each with a 3/8 in. cable embedded 12 in. deep forming a loop 4 in. above the block (8 req.). The pole is bolted to the plate with 1-1/8 in. x 4 in. hex. head bolts, hex. nuts and flat washers (4 req.), and 4 in. x 4 in. x 1/4 in. plate washers (4 req.). A 1/4 in. weld is shown typical. A level indicator is shown on the plate.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Signal, Temporary for Type CD954 Std. (Without Luminaire Arm), drawing number S-57.2C, approved August 8, 1984, Donald R. Howery, General Manager. Structural design checked 8-7-84 by P. H. Skarin, Div. Engr. Revisions list through 12-07-07 (updated mast arm head clearance and reference to standard drawings). Page number 40.
notes:
1. The CD954 standard (without luminaire arm) shall conform to Dept. of Transportation, City of Los Angeles, standard dwg. # S-51.9.6 (foundation excluded).
2. The mast arm length shall not exceed 15'-0".
3. There shall be a maximum of 2 - 5 section signal heads and 2 - ped. heads mounted to the shaft and one 5-section signal head mounted at the end of mast arm.
Callouts: Tie with 3/8 in. coil chain. 60 in. x 60 in. Weld angles to plate, 5 in. x 3 in. x 1/2 in. typical (revision 1). 23 in. x 23 in. x 30 in. precast conc. block (4 req.). 23 in. x 13 in. x 30 in. precast conc. block (4 req.). 2 in. hole. Drill holes (4 req.) to accommodate 1-1/8 in. bolt size and 11-1/2 in. bolt circle. 3/8 in. cable, embed 12 in. deep (8 req.). Type CD954 std. (revision 2). 1-1/8 in. x 4 in. hex. hd. bolt, hex. nut, flat washer (4 req.). Weld bolts and 4 in. x 4 in. x 1/4 in. plate washer to 3/4 in. plate (revision 1). Mortar leveling bed, wedge edges until mortar sets. (Mortar is not required on C.A.B., dirt or when slope is less than 1/4 in. per ft.) 60 in. x 60 in. x 3/4 in. steel plate. Coat plate assembly with primer and traffic signal yellow paint (revision 1). Temporary O.H. signal wires (maximum span 100 feet). All 12 in. sections. 15'-0" max. 17'-6" min. 2 signal heads. Street name sign. 2 pedestrian heads. See plan and Section A-A. Roadway. Type CD 954 Std. (without luminaire arm) (revision 2).
title: Signal, Temporary for Type CD954 Standard (Without Luminaire Arm)
summary: Drawing S-57.2C shows a temporary traffic signal on a Type CD954 standard without a luminaire arm. It sits on a 60 in. steel plate with eight precast concrete blocks, 3/8 in. cable loops and a 3/8 in. coil chain, with a mast arm up to 15 ft long and 17 ft 6 in. min. head clearance. Plan, elevation and Section A-A are given with three notes.

description:
Plan view: a 60 in. x 60 in. square footing assembly seen from above, made of precast concrete blocks laid in a 3 x 3 grid around the pole. Four 23 in. x 23 in. x 30 in. precast concrete blocks (4 req.) are at the corners and four 23 in. x 13 in. x 30 in. precast concrete blocks (4 req.) are at the middle of each side. 5 in. x 3 in. x 1/2 in. steel angles are welded to the plate at the corners and side midpoints (typical). A dashed square marks the 3/8 in. coil chain tie. Called out at the pole center: a 2 in. hole, and 4 in. x 4 in. x 1/2 in. plate washers (4 req.). Four 1-1/2 in. diameter holes are drilled for the 1-1/8 in. bolt size on an 11-1/2 in. bolt circle. Dimensions of 6 in. are shown at the center block and side. Section marks A and A are on both sides.

Elevation: a Type CD954 standard with a 4'-0" luminaire arm at the top and a mast arm 15'-0" max. long carrying one all-12 in. section signal head. Temporary overhead (O.H.) signal cable (maximum span 100 feet) is looped at the pole top. A vertical dimension of 17'-6" min. runs from the roadway to the mast arm head. Signal heads (see Note 3), 12 in. sections, are on the shaft, with a street name sign and 2 pedestrian heads below. A callout reads See Plan and Section A-A. A hatched roadway line is shown at grade.

Section A-A: a vertical cut through the base. A 60 in. x 60 in. x 3/4 in. steel plate sits on A.C. or P.C.C. surface on a mortar leveling bed, with a 1/4 in. weld typical. Blocks stand 30 in. high with 3/8 in. cable embedded 12 in. deep, forming loops 4 in. high (8 req.). The pole is bolted with 1-1/8 in. x 4 in. hex. hd. bolt, hex. nut, flat washer (4 req.) and 4 in. x 4 in. x 1/2 in. plate washers (4 req.). A level indicator is shown on the plate.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Signal, Temporary for Type CD954 Std., drawing number S-57.2D, approved 2-18-97 by Robert R. Yates, General Manager. Structural design checked 8-29-96 by C. W. Robins, Div. Engr. Page number 41.
notes:

title: Signal, Temporary for Type CD954 Standard (With Luminaire Arm)
summary: Drawing S-57.2D shows a temporary signal on a Type CD954 standard with a 4 ft luminaire arm and a mast arm up to 15 ft long. The base is a 60 in. x 60 in. x 3/4 in. steel plate with eight precast concrete blocks, cable loops and a coil chain. Plan, elevation, Section A-A and three notes are given, with 17 ft 6 in. min. head clearance.

description:
Elevation: a Type 8 standard carrying a 337 cabinet (traffic signal controller cabinet), drawn with the pole cut by break marks. The cabinet is a tall rectangular enclosure with a door handle, ventilation louvers and a City of Los Angeles label plate on the door. It sits on top of the pole and is called out as 337 Cabinet. At the bottom, two 5 gal. concrete blocks sit on a platform with a 3/8 in. diameter steel coil chain tied to each block and locked around the Type 8 standard. The base assembly is bolted to the platform, which has a 2 in. high lip and a LADOT name, a 1 in. x 1 in. notch for cable, and a note for slopes greater than 1/2 in. rise per foot.

Platform, top view detail (not to scale): a 36 in. x 36 in. square steel platform with four 5 gal. cans at the corners, a Type 1 base at the center with 4 bolts, and chain tied through the cans around the standard. Platform, bottom view detail (not to scale): 36 in. x 36 in. with steel angle brackets framing the underside, 4 holes at 1-1/4 in. diameter on an 8-1/2 in. diameter bolt circle, and 1 in. x 1 in. notches for cable at the lip.

Weight block (not to scale): a 5 gal. can filled with concrete, 12 in. wide by 14 in. tall, with a 1/2 in. diameter steel rod loop embedded 9 in. deep at 4 in. spacing and 3 in. above the can. Minimum weight 90 lbs. LADOT or contractor name is embossed or welded on at least two sides.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Temporary Controller for Type 8 Standard, sheet 1 of 1, drawing number S-57.3, drawn 3-1-16, approved 4-11-16 by Seleta J. Reynolds, General Manager. Page number 42.
notes:
1. 36 in. square (SQ.) x 1/4 in. thick (THK.) steel platform, hot dip galvanized per ASTM 123.
2. Type 1 base with 4 1 in. diameter x 3-1/2 in. bolts and nuts with 2 washers for each bolt.
3. 3/8 in. diameter steel coil chain tied to each 5 gal. block and locked around the Type 8 standard (and the Type 1 base in the top view detail).
4. 5 gal. can filled with concrete. Four cans are required, spaced as shown.
5. 2 in. high x 1/4 in. thick perimeter lip resting on ground.
6. 1-3/4 in. x 1-3/4 in. x 1/4 in. steel angle brackets welded to plate.
7. 4 holes at 1-1/4 in. diameter. 8-1/2 in. diameter bolt circle.
8. 1 in. x 1 in. notches for cable.
9. For slopes greater than 1/2 in. rise per foot, temporary standard to be set level through the use of grading or wood shims.
10. Weight block: 5 gal. can filled with concrete, minimum weight 90 lbs. 1/2 in. diameter steel rod embedded 9 in. deep. LADOT or contractor name embossed or welded on at least two sides.
Label: 337 cabinet. Base assembly. Lip.
title: Temporary Controller for Type 8 Standard
summary: Drawing S-57.3 shows a 337 controller cabinet mounted on a Type 8 standard for temporary use, held down by a 36 in. square steel platform and four 5 gallon concrete-filled cans chained around the pole. It gives the platform plan and underside layouts, bolt circle, lip and notches and a weight block detail of at least 90 lbs. It requires leveling on slopes steeper than 1/2 in. per foot.

description:
Slip fitter: an isometric view of a cylindrical slip fitter that slides over a post top. It is a stack of two round collars, an upper and a lower, on a central cylinder, with a smaller round post top projecting from the upper surface. The top rim of the projecting post has a toothed edge with 72 teeth. Two square-head set screws are shown on the side at the upper and lower collars. A callout reads 3/8 in.-16 N.C. x 3/4 in. square head cup point set screw, hot dip galvanized, (6) required.

Lock ring: an isometric view of a ring with a toothed upper rim of 72 teeth, an inner bore with two keyed notches on opposite sides, and a lower rim. A dimension of 5/16 in. is given for the ring height at the right.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Fittings, Typical, Post Top Mounting, drawing number S-61.1, drawn 2-67, revised 3-14-83, approved April 5, 1967 by A. L. Hutchison, Asst. General Manager. Page number 43.
notes:
1. Construction, material and finish painting shall conform to 'Standard Specifications', (latest edition), Dept. of Transportation, State of California.
Callouts: 72 teeth (slip fitter and lock ring). 3/8 in.-16 N.C. x 3/4 in. square head (Sq. Hd.) cup point (pt.) set screw, hot dip galvanized, (6) required (REQ.). Dimension 5/16 in.
title: Fittings, Typical, Post Top Mounting
summary: Drawing S-61.1 shows the typical post top mounting fittings, a slip fitter with six 3/8 in.-16 galvanized square head cup point set screws and a 72-tooth lock ring. The lock ring height is 5/16 in. One note requires construction, materials and finish painting to follow the State of California Standard Specifications.

description:
Pole clamp: an isometric view of a pole clamp, a 5/8 in. U-bolt with two slotted ear plates and nuts on the threaded ends, wrapped around a clamp casting with a 1-1/2 in. threaded center boss. The threaded ends are labeled Min. thread length 4 in.

Condulet-TB: an isometric view of a T-shaped conduit body with a removable cover plate fixed by two screws, and a threaded nipple stub. A callout reads 3-1/2 in. length nipple typical for 2-way heads.

Lock ring: an isometric view of a ring with a 72-tooth toothed rim and two keyed notches.

Special 90 degree elbow: an isometric view of an elbow with 1-1/2 in. pipe threads at both ends, one end having a 72-tooth toothed rim.

Special tee: an isometric view of a tee with 1-1/2 in. pipe threads at its ends and a 72-tooth toothed rim on the branch.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Fittings, Typical, Clamp Mounting, drawing number S-62.1, drawn 2-67, revised 3-14-83, approved April 5, 1967 by A. L. Hutchison, Asst. General Manager. Page number 44.
notes:
1. Construction, material and finish painting shall conform to 'Standard Specifications' (latest edition), Dept. of Transportation, State of California.
Callouts: 5/8 in. U-bolt. Min. thread length 4 in. 3-1/2 in. length nipple typical for 2-way heads. 72 teeth (lock ring, special 90 degree elbow and special tee). 1-1/2 in. pipe threads (special 90 degree elbow and special tee).
title: Fittings, Typical, Clamp Mounting
summary: Drawing S-62.1 shows typical clamp-mounting fittings for signal heads. They are a pole clamp with a 5/8 in. U-bolt, a Condulet-TB body with a 3-1/2 in. nipple, a 72-tooth lock ring, and a special 90 degree elbow and special tee with 1-1/2 in. pipe threads. One note requires State of California Standard Specifications.

description:
Terminal compartment, side-mount: an isometric view of a terminal compartment attached to the side of a pole, with a cover held by screws. It is fixed to the pole with 5/8 in.-11 N.C. hex. hd. bolts with lock washer and flat washer, hot dip galvanized, with flat washers and curved washers inside the pole. A 1/2 in. (min. thread) hub is called out at the side.

Terminal compartment, post-top mount: an isometric view of a terminal compartment on a slip fitter with two collars and 3/8 in.-16 N.C. x 3/4 in. sq. hd. cup pt. set screws, hot dip galvanized (6 Req.).

Lock ring, special tee and special 90 degree elbow: three isometric fitting views, each with a 72-tooth toothed rim. The tee and elbow have 1-1/2 in. pipe threads.

Washer detail A: a plan and edge view of a washer curved to fit the standard, with a 3/4 in. diameter hole and a 1-3/4 in. overall dimension.

Pole plate for side mountings: a section through the signal standard wall showing a pole plate with 1-1/2 in. pipe thread hub, held by two 5/8 in.-11 N.C. hex. hd. bolts, hot dip galvanized, with flat washers and Washers Detail A inside the pole and a 5/8 in. nut, 5/8 in. lockwasher and 5/8 in. flat washer outside. Dimensions are 1/2 in. (min. thds.) bolt thread projection and 5/16 in. plate thickness. A callout reads Cable guide - omit on upper plate.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Fittings, Typical, Terminal Compartment and Pole Plate Mounting, drawing number S-63.1, drawn 11-02-11, approved 12-8-11 by Jaime de la Vega, General Manager. Page number 45.
notes:
1. Construction, material and finish painting shall conform to 'Standard Specifications' (latest edition), Dept. of Transportation, State of California.
Callouts: 5/8 in.-11 N.C. hex. hd. bolt with lock washer and flat washer, hot dip galvanized. Flat washer and curved washer. 1/2 in. (min. thread). Cover. 3/8 in.-16 N.C. x 3/4 in. sq. hd. cup pt. set screw, hot dip galvanized (6 Req.). 72 teeth. 1-1/2 in. pipe threads. Washer curved to fit standard, 3/4 in. diameter, 1-3/4 in. Washer Detail A. Cable guide - omit on upper plate. 1/2 in. (min. thds.). 1-1/2 in. pipe thread. 5/8 in. nut. 5/8 in. lockwasher and 5/8 in. flat washer. Signal standard. 5/16 in.
title: Fittings, Typical, Terminal Compartment and Pole Plate Mounting
summary: Drawing S-63.1 shows typical fittings for signal standards. They are side-mount and post-top terminal compartments, a lock ring, special tee and 90 degree elbow, a curved washer (Detail A) and a pole plate for side mountings, all with 5/8 in. galvanized bolts and 1-1/2 in. pipe threads. One note requires State of California Standard Specifications.

description:
Item A (Pelco AB-3008): an isometric view of a mast arm mounting with a 6 in. long tenon, 2 3/8 in. outside diameter, held by two straps (bands) on a clamp.

Item B (Pelco AB-116): an exploded isometric view of a vertical gusseted tube with vinyl insert (typical), a bottom arm fixed to the tube with set screws (typical) and an upper arm that slides along the tube, with bolts, washers and round plates, and a toothed fitting at the arm end. Item E clamp (typical) is shown fastening the tube to a pole.

Item C (Pelco AB-103): a similar vertical tube with arms, long 14 in. arms, a toothed end, bolts and plates, and Item E clamp.

Item D (Pelco AB-0129 T-L) (modified): a vertical tube with arms with elbows at the top and bottom, aluminum lock nuts, square plates (Detail A, see Note No. 10) and 1-1/2 in. lock nuts (see Note No. 9), clamped to a pole with Item E.

Item E (Pelco AB-3004): an exploded view of a standard clamp kit with two U-bolts, nuts, washers, a clamp plate and two straps.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Special Mast Arm Mountings, sheet 1 of 2, drawing number S-63.1.4, drawn 5-12-98, approved May 27, 1998 by Thomas Conner, General Manager (Thomas K. Conner). Page number 46. Notes are on sheet 2.
notes: Callouts: 6 in. tenon length, 2 3/8 in. diameter. Item A (Pelco AB-3008). Gusseted tube with vinyl insert (typical). Item E (typical). Set screws (typical). Item B (Pelco AB-116). Item C (Pelco AB-103). Item D (Pelco AB-0129 T-L) (modified). Item E (Pelco AB-3004). See Note No. 9. Detail A, see Note No. 10. The numbered notes continue on sheet 2 (page 54).
title: Special Mast Arm Mountings (Sheet 1 of 2)
summary: Sheet 1 of 2 of drawing S-63.1.4 shows five Pelco mast arm signal mounting items, A through E, as isometric views. Item A is a 6 in. tenon mount, B and C are vertical arm mounts for signal heads, D is for electric signs and E is the standard clamp kit. The numbered notes are on sheet 2.

description:
Notes 1 to 10: ten notes describing mounting items A through E. They are listed in the notes field.

Detail A, 4 1/2 in. x 4 1/2 in. x 1/4 in. aluminum plate (not to scale): a square plate in plan, 4 1/2 in. by 4 1/2 in. It has four 3/8 in. diameter holes near the corners, each 3/4 in. typical from the edges, a central 2 in. diameter hole, and a 0.4 in. x 0.2 in. slot at the side of the central hole.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Special Mast Arm Mountings, sheet 2 of 2, drawing number S-63.1.4, drawn 5-7-98, approved May 27, 1998 by Thomas Conner, General Manager. Page number 47.
notes:
1. Item A is the basic mounting design for most mast arm signal installations when standard tenon location on the mast arm cannot be utilized. It uses a 6 in. tenon length with 2 3/8 in. outside diameter for plumbizer mounting.
2. Item B is used for installation of traffic signal heads, except programmed visibility (P.V.) heads, when it is desired to mount them horizontally or to adjust the height vertically by movement of Item E.
3. Item C is used for installation of horizontal or vertical programmed visibility (P.V.) heads. It is equipped with 14 in. arms which allow for replacement of signal lamps located in the rear of the signal head.
4. Item D is used for installation of electric signs.
5. Item E is a standard clamp kit designed to be used for fastening Items B, C and D to mast arms or poles in a vertical or horizontal position.
6. The bottom arms in Items B, C and D are stationary and are held in place with pipe threads and set screws. The upper arms slide along the shaft and are held in place with set screws.
7. The standard 29 in. band for Item A and E fits a 4 in. to 8.6 in. diameter. Band lengths up to 56 in. can be used for larger diameter installations.
8. Items A through E are available from Pelco Products Inc. or equivalent.
9. The 1 1/2 in. x 1 1/2 in. aluminum lock nut shown with Item D is commonly used for signal head and pedestrian head installations.
10. The 4 1/2 in. x 4 1/2 in. x 1/4 in. aluminum plate is used for sign box reinforcement at bracket installation location and must be specially fabricated.
Detail A: 4 1/2 in. x 4 1/2 in. x 1/4 in. aluminum plate, not to scale. 3/4 in. typical. 0.4 in. x 0.2 in. slot. 2 in. diameter hole. 3/8 in. diameter holes.
title: Special Mast Arm Mountings (Sheet 2 of 2)
summary: Sheet 2 of 2 of drawing S-63.1.4 gives ten notes on the Pelco mast arm mounting items A through E, covering their uses, band sizes and fabrication. Detail A is the 4 1/2 in. square, 1/4 in. aluminum plate with four 3/8 in. holes, a 2 in. center hole and a slot, used for sign box reinforcement.

description:
Plumbizer: an isometric view of a plumbizer mast arm bracket, a long arm with a threaded round hub at one end, a hollow tubular body with a slot and a clamp collar at the other end. Callouts: 3/8 in.-16 N.C. x 3/4 in. sq. hd. cup pt. set screw, hot dip galvanized, and 3/8 in.-16 N.C. x 4 in. sq. hd. bolt with 2 nuts and 2 flatwashers, hot dip galvanized.

Slip fitter: an isometric view of a 90 degree elbow-shaped slip fitter with a socket end on the side and a toothed end at the bottom with 72 teeth. Callouts: 3/8 in.-16 N.C. x 3/4 in. sq. hd. cup pt. set screw, hot dip galvanized, (2) Req., and the bolt and nut for the clamp.

Typical raintight connector: an exploded isometric view of a pole shaft with a slot, a keyed round plug and a raintight connector body with a threaded hole. A dashed line joins the parts with a special screw, 1/2 in.-13NC x 3/4 in., modified hex. head, hot dip galvanized.

Lock ring: an isometric view of a 72-tooth lock ring with two keyed notches, 5/16 in. high.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Fittings, Mast Arm Mounting, drawing number S-67.1, drawn 2-67, revised 3-14-83, approved April 5, 1967 by A. L. Hutchison, Asst. General Manager. Page number 48.
notes:
1. Construction, material and finish painting shall conform to 'Standard Specifications' (latest edition), Dept. of Transportation, State of California.
Callouts: 3/8 in.-16 N.C. x 3/4 in. sq. hd. cup pt. set screw, hot dip galvanized, (2) Req. 3/8 in.-16 N.C. x 4 in. sq. hd. bolt with 2 nuts and 2 flatwashers, hot dip galvanized. 72 teeth. Special screw 1/2 in.-13NC x 3/4 in. modified hex. head, hot dip galvanized. 5/16 in. Views: Plumbizer, Slip Fitter, Typical Raintight Connector, Lock Ring.
title: Fittings, Mast Arm Mounting
summary: Drawing S-67.1 shows mast arm mounting fittings: a plumbizer bracket, a 72-tooth slip fitter, a typical raintight connector with a special 1/2 in.-13NC screw and a lock ring. Bolt and set screw sizes are listed, all hot dip galvanized. One note requires State of California Standard Specifications.

description:
Plate elevation: a flat steel plate with a rounded top, drawn with its vertical centerline marked as symmetrical (CL SYMM.). The top end has a 1 1/4 in. radius and a 1 in. diameter hole at the center of the radius. Two 7/16 in. diameter holes are located 4 1/4 in. below the hole center, 3/4 in. each side of the centerline (1 1/2 in. apart). The plate extends 1 in. below the hole row. Drawn at scale 1/2 in. = 1 in.

Side section: the plate edge-on, 1/8 in. (stock) thick, drawn against the controller cabinet wall (ref.), with a 3/8 in. x 1 1/4 in. N.C. hex head bolt and nut, cad. plated (2 Req.) through the lower hole. A callout reads Drill four (4) 7/16 in. holes to match removable lifting plate.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Removable Lifting Plate for Controller Cabinets, drawing number S-68.1, drawn 9-27-83, approved October 3, 1983 by Donald R. Howery, General Manager. Page number 49.
notes:
1. Material: ASTM A36 steel plate.
2. Hot dip galvanized plate per ASTM Spec. A-123.
Callouts: 1 1/4 in. R. 1 in. Dia. Hole. 4 1/4 in. 1 in. 3/4 in. 1 1/2 in. 7/16 in. Dia. holes. Drill four (4) 7/16 in. holes to match removable lifting plate. 3/8 in. x 1 1/4 in. N.C. Hex. Head Bolt and nut, Cad. plated (2 Req.). 1/8 in. (Stock). Controller Cabinet Wall (Ref.). Scale: 1/2 in. = 1 in.
title: Removable Lifting Plate for Controller Cabinets
summary: Drawing S-68.1 gives the removable lifting plate for controller cabinets, a 1/8 in. galvanized A36 steel plate with a 1 1/4 in. radius end, a 1 in. lifting hole and two 7/16 in. bolt holes bolted to the cabinet wall with 3/8 in. x 1 1/4 in. cad plated bolts. The cabinet wall is drilled with four 7/16 in. holes to match.

description:
Side view of the visor: a cylindrical visor cut at an angle, shown as an elevation, 18 in. +/- 1/16 in. long along the top and 8 in. +/- 1/16 in. long along the bottom, with a dashed hidden line inside and small tabs at the open end. A centerline runs along the axis.

Left beveled view: a plan view of the visor with an elliptical opening, 8 1/8 in. +/- 1/16 in. diameter, and a 3.5 degree bevel angle at the left end. The title below reads Left Beveled.

Ear detail: an enlarged view of an ear with a 3/4 in. +/- 1/32 in. overall width, a 3/8 in. +/- 1/32 in. dimension to the centerline, a 1/8 in. radius +/- 1/32 in. and a 3/8 in. radius +/- 1/32 in.

End view: a circle with four ears at 45 degree positions around the visor, 90 degrees between ears, called out See Ear Detail. Dimensions are 6 7/16 in. +/- 1/16 in. between ears and 8 15/16 in. +/- 1/16 in. diagonal across the ears, with 45 degrees to the vertical centerline.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Visor, 8 in. Dia., Beveled, drawing number S-76.3, drawn 1-04-11, approved January 26, 2011 by Amir Sedadi, Interim General Manager. Page number 50.

title: Visor, 8 in. Dia., Beveled
summary: Drawing S-76.3 gives the dimensions of an 8 in. diameter beveled signal visor. It is 18 in. long along the top and 8 in. along the bottom with a 3.5 degree bevel, four ears at 45 degree positions and tolerances of 1/16 in. A note says to bevel the opposite side for a right beveled visor and to see LADOT Purchase Specification 92-061-06.
